page: Google Cloud Platform ct6e-standard-1t is an accelerator-focused instance within the TPU Machines family. It provides 44 dedicated x86_64 virtual central processing units and 176 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. Machine acceleration is driven by an integrated Google TPU v6e processor equipped with 32 GB of dedicated accelerator memory.

The system architecture pairs general-purpose host compute with Google custom ASIC hardware tailored for matrix operations. The ct6e-standard-1t includes no integrated local storage, requiring external storage volumes for operating system disks and data persistence. Connectivity includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring private VPC routing or provisioned external network routing.

This hardware profile delivers dedicated host resources sized to feed data pipelines directly into a single 32 GB TPU v6e device. It provides an efficient entry point for machine learning training, fine-tuning, and inference tasks optimized for Google Cloud TPU architectures, avoiding the operational complexity and resource overhead of multi-chip TPU topologies while maintaining sufficient host memory for data preprocessing.
description: Google Cloud Platform ct6e-standard-1t is an accelerator-equipped virtual machine within the TPU Machines family, designed for specialized machine learning tasks. The configuration features 44 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 176 GB of system memory, providing a consistent 4 GB of memory per core. Acceleration is handled by a single Google TPU v6e processor with 32 GB of accelerator memory for matrix execution. The instance contains no bundled local storage, relying on external network-attached storage volumes for operational storage needs. Furthermore, it does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The balanced ratio of host memory and compute cores to accelerator capacity ensures sufficient host-side throughput for ETL, batch preparation, and data feeding pipelines. This machine type serves as a targeted environment for model training, evaluation, and inference workloads tailored to Google Cloud TPU hardware without the scale requirements of multi-accelerator topologies.
